business_problem: Education Authority of Northern Ireland (EANI) faced challenges: varying student abilities requiring tailored educational approaches, limited resources in rural schools, administrative burdens on teachers, and rising complexity in special education needs necessitating better tools.
solution_summary: Students excel with Northern Ireland’s Microsoft Copilot integration Education Authority of Northern Ireland (EANI) faced challenges: varying student abilities requiring tailored educational approaches, limited resources in rural schools, administrative burdens on teachers, and rising complexity in special education needs necessitating better tools. Education Authority of Northern Ireland (EANI) introduced Microsoft Copilot to reduce admin work, allowing teachers to focus on students. The Microsoft partnership ensures secure and ethical AI use, while teacher training focuses on prompt writing and effective tool adoption. Through Copilot's innovative features, educators can now craft personalized learning experiences with ease. The technology adapts to diverse learning styles, ensuring every student has the opportunity to thrive, regardless of their challenges.

metrics: Established in 2015 under the Education Act, the Education Authority of Northern Ireland (EANI) is a regional body responsible for delivering education and youth services to approximately 1,200 schools, 21,000 teachers, and 380,000 students across the region. Their goal is to challenge, inspire, and empower students from pre-school through post-primary education.
